title: Special-Sense Organ Dynamics: Ocular Optics, Cochlear Frequency Analysis, and Vestibular Balance
abstract: The special-sense organs as physical instruments: one R19 bistable-channel transducer across vision, hearing, balance and taste; classical organ optics and acoustics; the cochlear Hopf cube-root; disease as basin collapse and therapy as its inverse.
headline_results: one R19 transducer across five senses

chapters.title: Special-sense organs emerge from measured DNA stiffness γ
chapters.one_liner: Six organ nodes are a γ-readout; the falsifiable order (taste latest) is confirmed.

chapters.title: Deterministic emergence: how the organs are derived from measured DNA, with no tuning
chapters.one_liner: LOCK → Derive → Gate: γ is measured, the order is derived, every page reproduces bit-for-bit.

chapters.title: The unified molecular transducer: every special sense is an R19 bistable channel switch
chapters.one_liner: Photoreceptor, hair-cell, and taste channels are all verified bistable double-wells.

chapters.title: Phototransduction: the rod CNG channel as a cooperative all-or-none switch
chapters.one_liner: Light shuts the cGMP-gated CNG channel; bistable flip, slope 3.32.

chapters.title: Ocular optics: the reduced eye, accommodation, and presbyopia
chapters.one_liner: Reduced eye reproduces axial 22.27 mm, 2.69 D/mm, presbyopia by Hofstetter.

chapters.title: Cochlear frequency analysis: the basilar-membrane place-map
chapters.one_liner: Greenwood place-map 19.8 Hz–20.7 kHz reproduced; the switch is the R19 MET gate.

chapters.title: The cochlear Hopf amplifier: parameter-free cube-root compression
Vestibular balance: the semicircular canal as a torsion pendulum
chapters.one_liner: Canal integrates acceleration to velocity over 0.1–6 Hz (flatness 0.018); VOR gain 1.0.

chapters.title: Chemodetection: taste and olfaction as threshold switches
chapters.one_liner: Taste GPCR opens TRPM5 (slope 3.12); olfaction shares the rod's CNG channel.

chapters.title: Disease as setpoint drift: the quadratic basin-collapse law
chapters.one_liner: Loop-gain drop d collapses the barrier as (g²/4)(1−d)²; rate rises monotonically.

chapters.title: Root-cause treatment: therapy as the inverse substrate operation
chapters.one_liner: Five inverse ops across seven diseases; a collapsed basin recovers 73% in the demo.

chapters.title: References, gene accessions, and methods provenance
chapters.one_liner: Every anchor, with its grade and database accession; substrate [V] reproduced, clinical [L] cited.
